theme.title: Rotation: Growth → Value & Defensives
theme.summary: Energy (-0.88%) and Consumer Staples (-1.40%) led the market today, while Consumer Discretionary (-3.19%) and Technology (-2.74%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -2.86% versus -1.65% for defensives and -1.60% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. Major indices moved in a tighter band — S&P 500 -2.00%, Dow -2.18%, Nasdaq -2.24% — without one clearly dominating. Small caps moved roughly in line with the broader market, with the Russell 2000 at -2.19%. The VIX rose 15.80% to 28.44, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 3.91% to $3,578.40, crude oil was little changed at $83.04, and bitcoin slipped 0.05% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
